subject: Hosted API — public wording for subprocessors & transfers
messages:
From: Acme Security <security@acme-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask — subprocessors & cross-border transfers for hosted API public page

Hi Karthik,

Following up from our procurement questionnaire — two items came up from legal that we hope you can put into plain English for our product/privacy teams so we can include them in our vendor assessment: 

1) We need a short, customer-facing paragraph that explains what "subprocessors" means for Redwood's Hosted API and whether customers can get a list of subprocessors on demand.
2) A concise explanation of how data may be transferred outside the EU (e.g., standard contractual clauses, adequacy, or other mechanisms) and what, if any, customer controls are available in the console (data residency selectors, export controls).

If you can share suggested copy (1-3 short sentences each) and any links to the subprocessor list or UI screenshots, that would be ideal.

Also copying Jane Doe from Acme procurement in case she wants to add context.

Thanks,

--
Acme Security
security@acme-analytics.com
Acme Analytics

Hi — thanks for the note and for flagging the specific asks. Looping in Kim and Laura (privacy product + console) and Marissa (policy copy) so we can put together short, customer-friendly snippets and point to the subprocessor list.

Plan: Kim and Marissa will propose UI text and a short FAQ-style explanation; Laura will confirm the console controls we can call out publicly (data residency selector, on-demand export request). I will consolidate and send back to you by EOD.

Two questions for clarity:
- Do you want the copy to live in the public privacy page only, or also in a Vendor FAQ (shorter) and the Console help tooltip (very short)?
- Is having a link to the up-to-date subprocessor list in the public privacy page sufficient, or does procurement require an emailed PDF snapshot?

Karthik

Thanks for looping us in. Attached are three short options for public-facing language (very UI-friendly) and an internal checklist for what the console can show. See attachments: ui_snippet_drafts.md and data_flow_diagram_v2.png (diagram stub).

Draft snippets (pick one or mix):

Option A (concise):
"Redwood may engage trusted third-party vendors (subprocessors) to help deliver the Hosted API. We publish an up-to-date list of subprocessors and will notify customers of major changes."

Option B (plain-English + control):
"Subprocessors are vendors we use to run the Hosted API (for example: cloud hosting, logging, and monitoring). You can view our current subprocessor list at the link below. If you need a snapshot for procurement, request one from contracts@redwood.com."

Option C (console-focused):
"Where available, customers can select a data residency region in the Console and request a subprocessor snapshot for audits. See the Privacy & Security section in Console settings."

Data transfer short paragraph (suggested):
"Data processed by the Hosted API may be transferred outside your region to operate the service. Transfers rely on recognized safeguards (EU Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent mechanisms). Customers can choose regional hosting where available; contact sales or support for options in regulated environments."

Notes: keep the UI tooltip < 160 characters; privacy page can be slightly longer. I added a one-line procurement fallback telling them to request the PDF if that is required.

Kim
Senior Product Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ui_snippet_drafts.md (markdown stub), data_flow_diagram_v2.png (image stub)

Jane / Acme team — attaching the suggested copy below. We aimed for short, procurement-friendly wording and a clear path if you need a certificate or a static snapshot for audit. If this looks good, we'll publish the "Option B" wording on the public privacy page and add the console-short version to the Privacy & Security help tooltip.

Suggested public privacy copy (Option B) — publishable verbatim:
"Subprocessors are vendors we use to operate the Hosted API (for example: cloud hosting, logging, and monitoring). We publish an up-to-date list of subprocessors at https://redwood.example.com/privacy/subprocessors. If you require a static snapshot for procurement, request one from contracts@redwood.com and we will provide a dated PDF for your records."

Suggested transfers sentence (publishable):
"Data processed by the Hosted API may be transferred outside your region to operate the service. Transfers rely on recognized safeguards (for EU customers we use EU Standard Contractual Clauses or equivalent mechanisms). Where available, customers may select a regional hosting option in the Console; contact sales@redwood.com for enterprise residency options."

Next steps:
- Acme: confirm if the link + snapshot flow meets procurement needs, or if they'd prefer an emailed PDF as a standing deliverable.
- Internal: we'll update the privacy page and Console help tooltip once Acme confirms.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Director, Contracts & Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference
